reason: PSD, AI and alpha PNG support is exactly what my fast viewer doesn't give me, so I'd install the portable zip and throw my own files at it. But one dev, v0.4.1, and nothing said about signing or source, so I won't hand it the default slot yet.
why_switch_or_not: 26 of 32 formats with PSD/AI/SVG/EXR/TGA in there is the kind of thing that makes me switch, since my viewer just shows nothing for half my work files. What stops me making it the default is that it's an unknown exe from one person with no mention of a signed build or open source, and I'd want to see it survive my 200k-picture drive (gallery, folder tree) before trusting it with every double-click. I'd keep my current viewer as default and open NuViewer for the PSD/AI/alpha stuff.
current_app_pros: Opens instantly, tiny footprint, I know the keys by heart, and it never gets in my way for plain JPG/PNG browsing.
current_app_pains: Can't open PSD or AI at all, alpha PNGs on a flat background don't show how they really look, and I bounce to Photoshop or Explorer just to peek at a layered file. Otherwise nothing.
objection: Is an unknown .exe from a single developer safe? The page doesn't say it's signed or open source, and Windows SmartScreen will probably yell at me.
would_change_my_mind: A code-signed installer or published source, plus proof that PSD with alpha and AI files open correctly and quickly in a folder of tens of thousands of images.
